Synopsis:
    July JOLTS data showed job openings rose modestly to 7.271M (below the 7.300M forecast), with manufacturing driving gains but hiring falling sharply by 278K. June openings were revised down significantly. The labor market is described as stable but in a holding pattern. Fed Chair Warsh signaled more tightening work may be needed if inflation doesn't move toward the 2% target. Markets are pricing a ~66% probability of a 25bps hike at the Sept 15-16 meeting, with the Fed funds rate currently at 3.50%-3.75%. August payrolls report (due Friday) is expected to rebound after a surprise July decline.
